raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The routed-experts capturer (`--enable-return-routed-experts`) keeps one row per device KV slot, and `get_topk` reads a request's rows through `req_to_token`. With `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, a prefix that comes back from the host tier is loaded into new device slots, but its rows are not. The prefix rows of every host-tier hit therefore come from whatever request used those slots before. Nothing fails; the client just receives wrong routing for the cached part of the prompt.

On upstream main, 3,916 of 3,918 prefix rows of a host-tier hit differed from the cold run of the same prompt (H100, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B`).

## Modifications

- New `mem_cache/hicache_topk_rows.py` (`HostTopkRows`), created by `HiCacheController` only when the routed-experts capturer exists.
  - The capturer allocates (and frees in `destroy()`) a host-tier rows buffer with its own host allocator: `host_kv_tokens x layers x top_k x 4 B` (Qwen3-30B-A3B: 0.09 GB for a 65,600-token host pool, logged at startup as `HostCache[routed_experts_hicache]`).
  - `start_writing` / `start_loading` copy the transfer's slot indices to the host on the transfer engine's index stream (after the stream that produced them, never behind earlier KV copies), and attach the resulting `TopkRowCopy` to the transfer's `HiCacheAck`.
  - When a write ack is processed (before the device slots can be freed), the rows of its device slots are copied to its host slots. When a load ack is processed, the rows of its host slots are copied into the new device slots. `get_topk` first applies any load not yet acked (a pre-read hook on the capturer); it waits for the index copies of pending loads, which run on the index stream after the work that produced the indices, not for the KV transfers. A load is applied once.
  - `HiCacheController.reset()` (cache flush) drops pending loads with the queues.
- `UnifiedRadixCache.writing_check` / `loading_check` and the PD decode KV offload manager apply the row copy carried by each processed ack.
- Rows are not persisted to L3 storage backends: with `--hicache-storage-backend`, rows of prefix pages loaded from storage are stale. The server warns at startup and the HiCache best-practices page says so.
- Tests:
  - `test/registered/rl/test_return_routed_experts_hicache.py` (`extra-a`, `1-gpu-large`, est. 400 s): a host-tier hit returns the cold run's prefix rows. Fails on main.
  - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_topk_rows.py` (CUDA, `1-gpu-small`): rows come back in the new slots through the ack or the pre-read hook, an acked load is not reapplied, reset drops pending loads, the rows are freed with the capturer.

## Accuracy Tests

`Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B`, TP1, `--enable-return-routed-experts --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 4 --max-total-tokens 16384 --page-size 1`. Prompt A (3,919 tokens) cold, then 8 other long prompts that push A's prefix out of the device pool, then A again (a host-tier hit). Baseline `8d4e1ce4c7` and this PR on the same GPU in the same container.

| | upstream main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1x GB300 (`--moe-runner-backend triton`): cached prefix rows that differ from the cold run | 3,902 / 3,904 | 0 / 3,904 |
| 1x H100 (default MoE runner): same | 3,916 / 3,918 | 0 / 3,918 |
| Output ids of the warm run == cold run | yes | yes |

The generated tokens never depended on these rows; only the returned routed experts change, from wrong to right.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

With routed experts and HiCache on, a shared-prefix workload whose prefixes move between the device and host tiers, arms main / PR / PR / main, 2 runs per launch. 1x GB300 (`--moe-runner-backend triton`) at commit `2471219a91` of this PR, where the slot-index copy still ran on the transfer stream:

```
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
  --gsp-num-groups 32 --gsp-prompts-per-group 8 --gsp-system-prompt-len 2048 \
  --gsp-question-len 128 --gsp-output-len 64 --max-concurrency 16 --return-routed-experts
```

| | output tok/s (4 runs) | median |
|---|---|---|
| main `8d4e1ce4c7` | 917.6, 994.7, 985.5, 1002.8 | 990.1 |
| this PR | 979.1, 1023.7, 976.9, 1021.4 | 1000.3 |

Same bench on 1x H100 (default MoE runner), at `2471219a91` and at the final head `a4f1ff527d` (index copy on the index stream):

| | output tok/s (4 runs) | median |
|---|---|---|
| main `8d4e1ce4c7` (session 1) | 515.6, 487.1, 495.4, 455.4 | 491.3 |
| this PR at `2471219a91` | 496.2, 465.0, 481.3, 445.8 | 473.2 |
| main `8d4e1ce4c7` (session 2) | 567.8, 577.6, 572.1, 578.0 | 574.8 |
| this PR at `a4f1ff527d` | 567.1, 573.1, 565.5, 571.4 | 569.3 |

GB300: no measurable cost (+1.0 %, within the run spread). H100: -3.7 % at `2471219a91` and -1.0 % at the final head in the median, with overlapping ranges in both; the cost is the row copy at each write and load ack on the scheduler thread, paid only with `--enable-return-routed-experts`. Host memory: the rows mirror for a 65,600-token host pool is 0.09 GB (`HostCache[routed_experts_hicache]` in the server log). Without `--enable-return-routed-experts` nothing is allocated and the hooks are skipped.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). A "Returning Routed Experts" note on the HiCache best-practices page.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). BUGFIX evidence above; generated tokens are unchanged (no gsm8k run).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).


Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""Host-tier copies of the routed-experts capturer rows for the hierarchical
+cache.
+
+The routed-experts capturer keeps one row per device KV slot, and get_topk
+reads a request's rows through req_to_token. A HiCache load-back puts a prefix
+into new device slots, so without these copies the prefix rows read back would
+be whatever those slots held before. Every HiCache write copies the rows of its
+device slots to its host slots, and every load-back copies them into the new
+device slots.
+
+The slot indices reach the CPU with a non-blocking copy on the transfer
+engine's index stream, so they never wait behind earlier KV copies. Each
+transfer's TopkRowCopy rides on its HiCacheAck. A write's rows are copied when
+its ack is processed, before the device slots can be freed. A load's rows are
+copied when its ack is processed, or earlier when get_topk reads rows.
+"""
+
+import collections
+import logging
+from typing import Optional
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.state_capturer.base import BaseTopkCapturer
+from sglang.srt.state_capturer.routed_experts import get_global_experts_capturer
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class TopkRowCopy(msgspec.Struct):
+    event: torch.cuda.Event
+    device_indices_cpu: torch.Tensor
+    host_indices_cpu: torch.Tensor
+    # Keeps the device index tensor alive until the copy has run.
+    device_indices: torch.Tensor
+    applied: bool = False
+
+
+class HostTopkRows:
+    def __init__(self, host_size: int, capturer: BaseTopkCapturer, device: str):
+        # The global capturer is set once at model load and owns (and frees)
+        # the host-tier buffer.
+        self._capturer = capturer
+        self._host_tier = capturer.alloc_host_tier_cache(
+            num_tokens=host_size, device=device
+        )
+        # Submitted loads in ack order; get_topk applies the ones not yet acked.
+        self._pending_loads: collections.deque = collections.deque()
+        capturer.add_pre_read_hook(self.apply_pending_loads)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def create(
+        host_size: int, device: str, has_storage_backend: bool
+    ) -> Optional["HostTopkRows"]:
+        capturer = get_global_experts_capturer()
+        if capturer is None:
+            return None
+        if has_storage_backend:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Routed experts are not stored in the HiCache storage backend: "
+                "prefix pages loaded from storage return stale routed-experts rows."
+            )
+        return HostTopkRows(host_size=host_size, capturer=capturer, device=device)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def copy_indices(
+        device_indices: torch.Tensor, host_indices: torch.Tensor, stream
+    ) -> TopkRowCopy:
+        """Copy the slot indices of a transfer to the host on stream (the
+        transfer engine's index stream), after the current stream that
+        produced them."""
+        device_indices_cpu = torch.empty(
+            device_indices.shape, dtype=device_indices.dtype, pin_memory=True
+        )
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            device_indices_cpu.copy_(device_indices, non_blocking=True)
+            event = torch.cuda.Event()
+            event.record(stream)
+        return TopkRowCopy(
+            event=event,
+            device_indices_cpu=device_indices_cpu,
+            host_indices_cpu=host_indices.cpu(),
+            device_indices=device_indices,
+        )
+
+    def add_load(self, row_copy: TopkRowCopy) -> None:
+        self._pending_loads.append(row_copy)
+
+    def finish_write(self, row_copy: TopkRowCopy) -> None:
+        """Copy the rows of the written device slots to their host slots."""
+        row_copy.event.synchronize()
+        self._host_tier.buffer[row_copy.host_indices_cpu] = (
+            self._capturer.host_cache.buffer[row_copy.device_indices_cpu]
+        )
+
+    def finish_load(self, row_copy: TopkRowCopy) -> None:
+        """Copy the rows of the loaded host slots into the new device slots."""
+        if not row_copy.applied:
+            row_copy.event.synchronize()
+            self._capturer.host_cache.buffer[row_copy.device_indices_cpu] = (
+                self._host_tier.buffer[row_copy.host_indices_cpu]
+            )
+            row_copy.applied = True
+        while self._pending_loads and self._pending_loads[0].applied:
+            self._pending_loads.popleft()
+
+    def apply_pending_loads(self) -> None:
+        for row_copy in list(self._pending_loads):
+            self.finish_load(row_copy)
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        self._pending_loads.clear()

+"""With --enable-hierarchical-cache, the routed experts of a prefix that comes
+back from the host tier must equal the rows of the cold run: prefix rows are
+reused on a cache hit, not recomputed."""
+
+import random
+import unittest
+
+import numpy as np
+import requests
+
+from sglang.srt.state_capturer.routed_experts import (
+    extract_routed_experts_from_meta_info,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils import kill_process_tree
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import (
+    DEFAULT_ENABLE_ROUTED_EXPERTS_MODEL_NAME_FOR_TEST,
+    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+    DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
+    CustomTestCase,
+    popen_launch_server,
+)
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=400, stage="extra-a", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+_NUM_LAYERS = 48
+_TOPK = 8
+_WORDS = "alpha bravo charlie delta echo foxtrot golf hotel india juliet kilo".split()
+
+
+def _long_prompt(seed: int, num_words: int = 2500) -> str:
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    words = " ".join(rng.choice(_WORDS) for _ in range(num_words))
+    return f"Document {seed}: {words}\nSummary:"
+
+
+class TestReturnRoutedExpertsHiCache(CustomTestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.process = popen_launch_server(
+            DEFAULT_ENABLE_ROUTED_EXPERTS_MODEL_NAME_FOR_TEST,
+            DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
+            timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+            other_args=[
+                "--enable-return-routed-experts",
+                "--enable-hierarchical-cache",
+                "--hicache-ratio",
+                4,
+                "--max-total-tokens",
+                16384,
+                "--page-size",
+                1,
+            ],
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def tearDownClass(cls):
+        kill_process_tree(cls.process.pid)
+
+    def _generate(self, text: str) -> dict:
+        resp = requests.post(
+            f"{DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST}/generate",
+            json={
+                "text": text,
+                "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 8},
+                "return_routed_experts": True,
+            },
+            timeout=300,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200, resp.text)
+        return resp.json()
+
+    def _rows(self, out: dict) -> np.ndarray:
+        return extract_routed_experts_from_meta_info(out).reshape(
+            -1, _NUM_LAYERS, _TOPK
+        )
+
+    def test_host_tier_hit_returns_cold_rows(self):
+        cold = self._generate(_long_prompt(seed=0))
+        # Fill the device pool so the first prompt's prefix moves to the host tier.
+        for seed in range(1, 9):
+            self._generate(_long_prompt(seed=seed))
+        warm = self._generate(_long_prompt(seed=0))
+
+        cached = warm["meta_info"]["cached_tokens"]
+        num_prefix_rows = min(cached, cold["meta_info"]["prompt_tokens"] - 1)
+        self.assertGreater(num_prefix_rows, 0, "expected a prefix cache hit")
+        cold_rows = self._rows(cold)[:num_prefix_rows]
+        warm_rows = self._rows(warm)[:num_prefix_rows]
+        mismatched = int((cold_rows != warm_rows).any(axis=(1, 2)).sum())
+        self.assertEqual(
+            mismatched,
+            0,
+            f"{mismatched} of {num_prefix_rows} cached prefix rows differ from the cold run",
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+"""HiCache keeps routed-experts rows with their KV: a write copies the rows of
+its device slots to host slots, and a load-back copies them into the new
+device slots before get_topk reads them."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_topk_rows import HostTopkRows
+from sglang.srt.state_capturer.base import BaseTopkCapturer
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+HOST_SLOTS = [10, 11, 12]
+
+
+@unittest.skipIf(not torch.cuda.is_available(), "needs CUDA")
+class TestHiCacheTopkRows(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.capturer = BaseTopkCapturer(
+            num_tokens=64,
+            max_batch_size=8,
+            num_layers=2,
+            topk_size=3,
+            device="cuda",
+            name="routed_experts",
+        )
+        self.rows = HostTopkRows(host_size=32, capturer=self.capturer, device="cuda")
+        self.stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        self.expected = torch.arange(18, dtype=torch.int32).view(3, 2, 3)
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        self.capturer.destroy()
+
+    def _copy(self, device_slots):
+        return HostTopkRows.copy_indices(
+            device_indices=torch.tensor(device_slots, device="cuda"),
+            host_indices=torch.tensor(HOST_SLOTS),
+            stream=self.stream,
+        )
+
+    def _write_prefix(self):
+        """Rows of device slots 5..7 are backed up to host slots 10..12, then
+        the device slots are reused by another request."""
+        self.capturer.host_cache.buffer[[5, 6, 7]] = self.expected
+        self.rows.finish_write(self._copy([5, 6, 7]))
+        self.capturer.host_cache.buffer[[5, 6, 7]] = -1
+
+    def _load(self, device_slots):
+        row_copy = self._copy(device_slots)
+        self.rows.add_load(row_copy)
+        return row_copy
+
+    def _read(self, slots):
+        pool = SimpleNamespace(
+            req_to_token=torch.tensor([slots + [0]], dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+        )
+        return self.capturer.get_topk(
+            req_pool_idx=0, seqlen=len(slots) + 1, req_to_token_pool=pool
+        )
+
+    def test_load_back_restores_rows_before_read(self):
+        self._write_prefix()
+        self._load([20, 21, 22])
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(self._read([20, 21, 22]), self.expected))
+
+    def test_load_ack_restores_rows_once(self):
+        self._write_prefix()
+        row_copy = self._load([30, 31, 32])
+        self.rows.finish_load(row_copy)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(self.capturer.host_cache.buffer[[30, 31, 32]], self.expected)
+        )
+        # The slots are reused before the next read; an acked load must not
+        # be applied again.
+        self.capturer.host_cache.buffer[[30, 31, 32]] = 7
+        self._read([30, 31, 32])
+        self.assertTrue((self.capturer.host_cache.buffer[[30, 31, 32]] == 7).all())
+
+    def test_reset_drops_pending_copies(self):
+        self._write_prefix()
+        self._load([40, 41, 42])
+        self.rows.reset()
+        self.rows.apply_pending_loads()
+        self.assertTrue((self.capturer.host_cache.buffer[[40, 41, 42]] == 0).all())
+
+    def test_host_tier_rows_are_freed_with_the_capturer(self):
+        self.assertIsNotNone(self.capturer.host_tier_cache.buffer)
+        self.capturer.destroy()
+        self.assertIsNone(self.capturer.host_tier_cache.buffer)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
